sanskrit: tato rudraś ca devī ca pāvakaś ca pitāmaham gaṅgayā sahitāḥ sarve praṇipetur jagatpatim
english: Then Rudra, and the Goddess, and Pāvaka, together with Gaṅgā—all of them bowed down before the Grandsire, the Lord of the world.

sanskrit: praṇipatya tatas te tu vidhivad rājapuṃgava idam ūcur vaco rājan kārttikeyapriyepsayā
english: Having made their obeisance in due form, O bull among kings, they then spoke these words, O king, in their wish to secure a boon for Kārttikeya:

sanskrit: asya bālasya bhagavann ādhipatyaṃ yathepsitam asmatpriyārthaṃ deveśa sadṛśaṃ dātum arhasi
english: "For this boy, O Lord, for our gratification, O Lord of the gods, it is fitting that you grant a sovereignty befitting him, such as he may desire."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bhagavān dhīmān sarvalokapitāmahaḥ manasā cintayām āsa kim ayaṃ labhatām iti
english: Then that wise and blessed Grandsire of all the worlds pondered in his mind: "What should be bestowed upon him?"

sanskrit: aiśvaryāṇi hi sarvāṇi devagandharvarakṣasām bhūtayakṣavihaṃgānāṃ pannagānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: For all the lordships of the gods, the gandharvas and the rākṣasas, of the spirits, the yakṣas, and the birds, and of the serpents in their entirety,

sanskrit: pūrvam evādideśāsau nikāyeṣu mahātmanām samarthaṃ ca tam aiśvarye mahāmatir amanyata
english: he had already ordained among the hosts of the great-souled ones; yet that one of vast wisdom deemed the boy fit for sovereignty.

sanskrit: tato muhūrtaṃ sa dhyātvā devānāṃ śreyasi sthitaḥ senāpatyaṃ dadau tasmai sarvabhūteṣu bhārata
english: Then, having reflected for a moment, intent upon the welfare of the gods, he bestowed upon him the office of commander over all beings, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sarvadevanikāyānāṃ ye rājānaḥ pariśrutāḥ tān sarvān vyādideśāsmai sarvabhūtapitāmahaḥ
english: All those who were renowned as kings among the several hosts of the gods—the Grandsire of all beings appointed them, every one, to his command.

sanskrit: tataḥ kumāram ādāya devā brahmapurogamāḥ abhiṣekārtham ājagmuḥ śailendraṃ sahitās tataḥ
english: Then the gods, led by Brahmā, taking the prince with them, came together to the king of mountains for the consecration.

sanskrit: puṇyāṃ haimavatīṃ devīṃ saricchreṣṭhāṃ sarasvatīm samantapañcake yā vai triṣu lokeṣu viśrutā
english: They came to the holy goddess sprung from Himavat, Sarasvatī, the best of rivers, who at Samantapañcaka is renowned throughout the three worlds.

sanskrit: tatra tīre sarasvatyāḥ puṇye sarvaguṇānvite niṣedur devagandharvāḥ sarve saṃpūrṇamānasāḥ
english: There upon the holy bank of the Sarasvatī, endowed with every excellence, the gods and gandharvas all took their seats, their hearts filled with contentment.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato 'bhiṣekasaṃbhārān sarvān saṃbhṛtya śāstrataḥ bṛhaspatiḥ samiddhe 'gnau juhāvājyaṃ yathāvidhi
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, having gathered together all the materials of the consecration according to scripture, Bṛhaspati poured clarified butter into the kindled fire as the rite ordained.

sanskrit: tato himavatā datte maṇipravaraśobhite divyaratnācite divye niṣaṇṇaḥ paramāsane
english: Then, seated upon a divine throne supreme, given by Himavat, gleaming with the choicest gems and studded with celestial jewels,

sanskrit: sarvamaṅgalasaṃbhārair vidhimantrapuraskṛtam ābhiṣecanikaṃ dravyaṃ gṛhītvā devatāgaṇāḥ
english: the hosts of the gods, taking up the materials of the consecration with all auspicious appurtenances, attended by the proper rites and sacred formulas,

sanskrit: indrāviṣṇū mahāvīryau sūryācandramasau tathā dhātā caiva vidhātā ca tathā caivānilānalau
english: Indra and Viṣṇu of mighty valour, the Sun and the Moon, Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ likewise, and Anila and Anala,

sanskrit: pūṣṇā bhagenāryamṇā ca aṃśena ca vivasvatā rudraś ca sahito dhīmān mitreṇa varuṇena ca
english: with Pūṣan, Bhaga, and Aryaman, with Aṃśa and Vivasvat, and the wise Rudra together with Mitra and Varuṇa—

sanskrit: rudrair vasubhir ādityair aśvibhyāṃ ca vṛtaḥ prabhuḥ viśvedevair marudbhiś ca sādhyaiś ca pitṛbhiḥ saha
english: the Lord surrounded by the Rudras, the Vasus, the Ādityas, and the two Aśvins, by the Viśvedevas and the Maruts, and by the Sādhyas together with the Fathers,

sanskrit: gandharvair apsarobhiś ca yakṣarākṣasapannagaiḥ devarṣibhir asaṃkhyeyais tathā brahmarṣibhir varaiḥ
english: by gandharvas and apsarases, by yakṣas, rākṣasas, and serpents, by countless divine sages and by the foremost brahmin sages,

sanskrit: vaikhānasair vālakhilyair vāyvāhārair marīcipaiḥ bhṛgubhiś cāṅgirobhiś ca yatibhiś ca mahātmabhiḥ sarvair vidyādharaiḥ puṇyair yogasiddhais tathā vṛtaḥ
english: by the Vaikhānasas and the Vālakhilyas, by those who feed on air and those who drink the rays of the sun, by the Bhṛgus and the Aṅgirases and the great-souled ascetics, and surrounded by all the holy vidyādharas perfected in yoga,

sanskrit: pitāmahaḥ pulastyaś ca pulahaś ca mahātapāḥ aṅgirāḥ kaśyapo 'triś ca marīcir bhṛgur eva ca
english: the Grandsire, and Pulastya, and Pulaha of great austerity, Aṅgiras, Kaśyapa, and Atri, Marīci and Bhṛgu,

sanskrit: kratur haraḥ pracetāś ca manur dakṣas tathaiva ca ṛtavaś ca grahāś caiva jyotīṃṣi ca viśāṃ pate
english: Kratu, Hara, and Pracetas, Manu and Dakṣa likewise, and the seasons, the planets, and the heavenly luminaries, O lord of peoples,

sanskrit: mūrtimatyaś ca sarito vedāś caiva sanātanāḥ samudrāś ca hradāś caiva tīrthāni vividhāni ca pṛthivī dyaur diśaś caiva pādapāś ca janādhipa
english: the rivers in embodied form, and the eternal Vedas, the seas and the lakes and the various sacred fords, the Earth, the Sky, and the quarters, and the trees, O ruler of men,

sanskrit: aditir devamātā ca hrīḥ śrīḥ svāhā sarasvatī umā śacī sinīvālī tathā cānumatiḥ kuhūḥ rākā ca dhiṣaṇā caiva patnyaś cānyā divaukasām
english: Aditi the mother of the gods, and Hrī, Śrī, Svāhā, and Sarasvatī, Umā, Śacī, Sinīvālī, and Anumati, Kuhū, and Rākā, and Dhiṣaṇā, and the other wives of the dwellers of heaven,

sanskrit: himavāṃś caiva vindhyaś ca meruś cānekaśṛṅgavān airāvataḥ sānucaraḥ kalāḥ kāṣṭhās tathaiva ca māsārdhamāsā ṛtavas tathā rātryahanī nṛpa
english: Himavat, and Vindhya, and Meru of many peaks, Airāvata with his followers, the moments and the divisions of time, the months and half-months, the seasons, and Night and Day, O king,

sanskrit: uccaiḥśravā hayaśreṣṭho nāgarājaś ca vāmanaḥ aruṇo garuḍaś caiva vṛkṣāś cauṣadhibhiḥ saha
english: Uccaiḥśravas, the best of horses, and Vāmana, the king of elephants, Aruṇa and Garuḍa, and the trees together with the healing herbs,

sanskrit: dharmaś ca bhagavān devaḥ samājagmur hi saṃgatāḥ kālo yamaś ca mṛtyuś ca yamasyānucarāś ca ye
english: and the divine Lord Dharma—all these assembled and came together, and Time, and Yama, and Death, and those who are Yama's followers.

sanskrit: bahulatvāc ca noktā ye vividhā devatāgaṇāḥ te kumārābhiṣekārthaṃ samājagmus tatas tataḥ
english: And the manifold hosts of deities not named here on account of their multitude came together from this place and that for the prince's consecration.

sanskrit: jagṛhus te tadā rājan sarva eva divaukasaḥ ābhiṣecanikaṃ bhāṇḍaṃ maṅgalāni ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Then, O king, all those dwellers of heaven took up the vessels of consecration and every auspicious object.

sanskrit: divyasaṃbhārasaṃyuktaiḥ kalaśaiḥ kāñcanair nṛpa sarasvatībhiḥ puṇyābhir divyatoyābhir eva tu
english: With golden jars filled with divine appurtenances, O king, and with the holy waters of the Sarasvatī, waters indeed celestial,

sanskrit: abhyaṣiñcan kumāraṃ vai saṃprahṛṣṭā divaukasaḥ senāpatiṃ mahātmānam asurāṇāṃ bhayāvaham
english: the dwellers of heaven, greatly rejoicing, consecrated the prince, the great-souled commander, the terror of the asuras.

sanskrit: purā yathā mahārāja varuṇaṃ vai jaleśvaram tathābhyaṣiñcad bhagavān brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ kaśyapaś ca mahātejā ye cānye nānukīrtitāḥ
english: As of old, O great king, Varuṇa the lord of waters was consecrated, even so did the blessed Brahmā, the Grandsire of the world, consecrate him, and Kaśyapa of great splendour, and the others not here recounted.

sanskrit: tasmai brahmā dadau prīto balino vātaraṃhasaḥ kāmavīryadharān siddhān mahāpāriṣadān prabhuḥ
english: To him Brahmā, well pleased, the Lord gave mighty attendants swift as the wind, perfected beings who bore valour at will, great companions of his retinue:

sanskrit: nandiṣeṇaṃ lohitākṣaṃ ghaṇṭākarṇaṃ ca saṃmatam caturtham asyānucaraṃ khyātaṃ kumudamālinam
english: Nandiṣeṇa, Lohitākṣa, and the esteemed Ghaṇṭākarṇa, and as his fourth follower, the renowned Kumudamālin.

sanskrit: tataḥ sthāṇuṃ mahāvegaṃ mahāpāriṣadaṃ kratum māyāśatadharaṃ kāmaṃ kāmavīryabalānvitam dadau skandāya rājendra surārivinibarhaṇam
english: Then, O lord of kings, Sthāṇu gave to Skanda the great companion Kratu of mighty force, and Kāma, wielder of a hundred illusions, endowed with strength and valour at will, the destroyer of the foes of the gods.

sanskrit: sa hi devāsure yuddhe daityānāṃ bhīmakarmaṇām jaghāna dorbhyāṃ saṃkruddhaḥ prayutāni caturdaśa
english: For he, in the war of the gods and the asuras, in his wrath slew with his two arms fourteen million of the daityas of dreadful deeds.

sanskrit: tathā devā dadus tasmai senāṃ nairṛtasaṃkulām devaśatrukṣayakarīm ajayyāṃ viśvarūpiṇīm
english: Likewise the gods gave him an army teeming with rākṣasas, that wrought the destruction of the gods' enemies, unconquerable and of every shape.

sanskrit: jayaśabdaṃ tataś cakrur devāḥ sarve savāsavāḥ gandharvayakṣarakṣāṃsi munayaḥ pitaras tathā
english: Then all the gods together with Vāsava raised the cry of victory, and the gandharvas, yakṣas, and rākṣasas, the sages, and the Fathers as well.

sanskrit: yamaḥ prādād anucarau yamakālopamāv ubhau unmāthaṃ ca pramāthaṃ ca mahāvīryau mahādyutī
english: Yama gave two followers, both like Yama and Time themselves, Unmātha and Pramātha, of mighty valour and great splendour.

sanskrit: subhrājo bhāskaraś caiva yau tau sūryānuyāyinau tau sūryaḥ kārttikeyāya dadau prītaḥ pratāpavān
english: Subhrāja and Bhāskara, the two who attend upon the Sun—those the glorious Sūrya, well pleased, gave to Kārttikeya.

sanskrit: kailāsaśṛṅgasaṃkāśau śvetamālyānulepanau somo 'py anucarau prādān maṇiṃ sumaṇim eva ca
english: Resembling the peak of Kailāsa, garlanded and anointed with white, Soma too gave two followers, Maṇi and Sumaṇi.

sanskrit: jvālājihvaṃ tathā jyotir ātmajāya hutāśanaḥ dadāv anucarau śūrau parasainyapramāthinau
english: Jvālājihva and Jyoti—these the Fire-god gave to his own son as followers, two heroes who crushed the armies of the foe.

sanskrit: parighaṃ ca vaṭaṃ caiva bhīmaṃ ca sumahābalam dahatiṃ dahanaṃ caiva pracaṇḍau vīryasaṃmatau aṃśo 'py anucarān pañca dadau skandāya dhīmate
english: Parigha and Vaṭa, and the mighty Bhīma, and Dahati and Dahana, fierce and esteemed for valour—these five followers Aṃśa too gave to the wise Skanda.

sanskrit: utkrośaṃ paṅkajaṃ caiva vajradaṇḍadharāv ubhau dadāv analaputrāya vāsavaḥ paravīrahā tau hi śatrūn mahendrasya jaghnatuḥ samare bahūn
english: Utkrośa and Paṅkaja, both bearing the thunderbolt and the rod, Vāsava the slayer of enemy heroes gave to the son of Agni; for these two had slain in battle many of great Indra's foes.

sanskrit: cakraṃ vikramakaṃ caiva saṃkramaṃ ca mahābalam skandāya trīn anucarān dadau viṣṇur mahāyaśāḥ
english: Cakra and Vikramaka, and the mighty Saṃkrama—these three followers Viṣṇu of great renown gave to Skanda.

sanskrit: vardhanaṃ nandanaṃ caiva sarvavidyāviśāradau skandāya dadatuḥ prītāv aśvinau bharatarṣabha
english: Vardhana and Nandana, both skilled in all the sciences, the two Aśvins, well pleased, gave to Skanda, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: kundanaṃ kusumaṃ caiva kumudaṃ ca mahāyaśāḥ ḍambarāḍambarau caiva dadau dhātā mahātmane
english: Kundana and Kusuma and Kumuda, and Ḍambara and Āḍambara—these the illustrious Dhātṛ gave to the great-souled one.

sanskrit: vakrānuvakrau balinau meṣavaktrau balotkaṭau dadau tvaṣṭā mahāmāyau skandāyānucarau varau
english: Vakra and Anuvakra, two mighty ones with ram-faces, swollen with strength and full of great illusion—Tvaṣṭṛ gave these excellent followers to Skanda.

sanskrit: suvrataṃ satyasaṃdhaṃ ca dadau mitro mahātmane kumārāya mahātmānau tapovidyādharau prabhuḥ
english: Suvrata and Satyasaṃdha, two great-souled bearers of austerity and sacred knowledge—the Lord Mitra gave to the great-souled prince.

sanskrit: sudarśanīyau varadau triṣu lokeṣu viśrutau suprabhaṃ ca mahātmānaṃ śubhakarmāṇam eva ca kārttikeyāya saṃprādād vidhātā lokaviśrutau
english: Fair to look upon, granters of boons, renowned throughout the three worlds—the great-souled Suprabhā and Śubhakarman, famed in the worlds, Vidhātṛ bestowed upon Kārttikeya.

sanskrit: pālitakaṃ kālikaṃ ca mahāmāyāvināv ubhau pūṣā ca pārṣadau prādāt kārttikeyāya bhārata
english: Pālitaka and Kālika, both masters of great illusion—these two attendants Pūṣan gave to Kārttikeya, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: balaṃ cātibalaṃ caiva mahāvaktrau mahābalau pradadau kārttikeyāya vāyur bharatasattama
english: Bala and Atibala, both great of mouth and great of strength, Vāyu gave to Kārttikeya, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: ghasaṃ cātighasaṃ caiva timivaktrau mahābalau pradadau kārttikeyāya varuṇaḥ satyasaṃgaraḥ
english: Ghasa and Atighasa, two of mighty strength with the faces of sea-monsters, Varuṇa, true to his pledge, gave to Kārttikeya.

sanskrit: suvarcasaṃ mahātmānaṃ tathaivāpy ativarcasam himavān pradadau rājan hutāśanasutāya vai
english: The great-souled Suvarcas, and likewise Ativarcas, Himavat gave, O king, to the son of the Fire-god.

sanskrit: kāñcanaṃ ca mahātmānaṃ meghamālinam eva ca dadāv anucarau merur agniputrāya bhārata
english: The great-souled Kāñcana and Meghamālin—these two followers Meru gave to the son of Agni, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sthiraṃ cātisthiraṃ caiva merur evāparau dadau mahātmane 'gniputrāya mahābalaparākramau
english: Sthira and Atisthira—two more Meru gave likewise to the great-souled son of Agni, both of great strength and prowess.

sanskrit: ucchritaṃ cātiśṛṅgaṃ ca mahāpāṣāṇayodhinau pradadāv agniputrāya vindhyaḥ pāriṣadāv ubhau
english: Ucchrita and Atiśṛṅga, two warriors who fought with great boulders, Vindhya gave to the son of Agni as his attendants.

sanskrit: saṃgrahaṃ vigrahaṃ caiva samudro 'pi gadādharau pradadāv agniputrāya mahāpāriṣadāv ubhau
english: Saṃgraha and Vigraha, both bearers of the mace, the Ocean too gave to the son of Agni, two great companions of his retinue.

sanskrit: unmādaṃ puṣpadantaṃ ca śaṅkukarṇaṃ tathaiva ca pradadāv agniputrāya pārvatī śubhadarśanā
english: Unmāda, Puṣpadanta, and Śaṅkukarṇa likewise—these Pārvatī, fair of aspect, gave to the son of Agni.

sanskrit: jayaṃ mahājayaṃ caiva nāgau jvalanasūnave pradadau puruṣavyāghra vāsukiḥ pannageśvaraḥ
english: Jaya and Mahājaya, two serpents, O tiger among men, Vāsuki the lord of serpents gave to the son of Fire.

sanskrit: evaṃ sādhyāś ca rudrāś ca vasavaḥ pitaras tathā sāgarāḥ saritaś caiva girayaś ca mahābalāḥ
english: Thus the Sādhyas and the Rudras, the Vasus and the Fathers, the seas and the rivers, and the mighty mountains,

sanskrit: daduḥ senāgaṇādhyakṣāñ śūlapaṭṭiśadhāriṇaḥ divyapraharaṇopetān nānāveṣavibhūṣitān
english: gave him captains over the hosts of his army, bearers of the lance and the spear, furnished with divine weapons and adorned in manifold guise.

sanskrit: śṛṇu nāmāni cānyeṣāṃ ye 'nye skandasya sainikāḥ vividhāyudhasaṃpannāś citrābharaṇavarmiṇaḥ
english: Hear now the names of the others, those who were Skanda's soldiers, furnished with manifold weapons and bright ornaments and armour:

sanskrit: śaṅkukarṇo nikumbhaś ca padmaḥ kumuda eva ca ananto dvādaśabhujas tathā kṛṣṇopakṛṣṇakau
english: Śaṅkukarṇa and Nikumbha, Padma and Kumuda, Ananta of twelve arms, and Kṛṣṇa and Upakṛṣṇaka,

sanskrit: droṇaśravāḥ kapiskandhaḥ kāñcanākṣo jalaṃdhamaḥ akṣasaṃtarjano rājan kunadīkas tamobhrakṛt
english: Droṇaśravas, Kapiskandha, Kāñcanākṣa, Jalaṃdhama, Akṣasaṃtarjana, O king, Kunadīka, and Tamobhrakṛt,

sanskrit: ekākṣo dvādaśākṣaś ca tathaivaikajaṭaḥ prabhuḥ sahasrabāhur vikaṭo vyāghrākṣaḥ kṣitikampanaḥ
english: Ekākṣa and Dvādaśākṣa, and Ekajaṭa the lordly, Sahasrabāhu, Vikaṭa, Vyāghrākṣa, and Kṣitikampana,

sanskrit: puṇyanāmā sunāmā ca suvaktraḥ priyadarśanaḥ pariśrutaḥ kokanadaḥ priyamālyānulepanaḥ
english: Puṇyanāman and Sunāman, Suvaktra and Priyadarśana, Pariśruta, Kokanada, and Priyamālyānulepana,

sanskrit: ajodaro gajaśirāḥ skandhākṣaḥ śatalocanaḥ jvālājihvaḥ karālaś ca sitakeśo jaṭī hariḥ
english: Ajodara, Gajaśiras, Skandhākṣa, Śatalocana, Jvālājihva, Karāla, Sitakeśa, Jaṭin, and Hari,

sanskrit: caturdaṃṣṭro 'ṣṭajihvaś ca meghanādaḥ pṛthuśravāḥ vidyudakṣo dhanurvaktro jaṭharo mārutāśanaḥ
english: Caturdaṃṣṭra and Aṣṭajihva, Meghanāda, Pṛthuśravas, Vidyudakṣa, Dhanurvaktra, Jaṭhara, and Mārutāśana,

sanskrit: udarākṣo jhaṣākṣaś ca vajranābho vasuprabhaḥ samudravego rājendra śailakampī tathaiva ca
english: Udarākṣa and Jhaṣākṣa, Vajranābha, Vasuprabha, Samudravega, O lord of kings, and Śailakampin likewise,

sanskrit: putrameṣaḥ pravāhaś ca tathā nandopanandakau dhūmraḥ śvetaḥ kaliṅgaś ca siddhārtho varadas tathā
english: Putrameṣa and Pravāha, and Nanda and Upanandaka, Dhūmra, Śveta, and Kaliṅga, Siddhārtha, and Varada,

sanskrit: priyakaś caiva nandaś ca gonandaś ca pratāpavān ānandaś ca pramodaś ca svastiko dhruvakas tathā
english: Priyaka and Nanda, and the valorous Gonanda, Ānanda and Pramoda, Svastika, and Dhruvaka likewise,

sanskrit: kṣemavāpaḥ sujātaś ca siddhayātraś ca bhārata govrajaḥ kanakāpīḍo mahāpāriṣadeśvaraḥ
english: Kṣemavāpa and Sujāta, and Siddhayātra, O Bhārata, Govraja, Kanakāpīḍa, the great lord of the retinue,

sanskrit: gāyano hasanaś caiva bāṇaḥ khaḍgaś ca vīryavān vaitālī cātitālī ca tathā katikavātikau
english: Gāyana and Hasana, Bāṇa and the valiant Khaḍga, Vaitālin and Atitālin, and Katika and Vātika,

sanskrit: haṃsajaḥ paṅkadigdhāṅgaḥ samudronmādanaś ca ha raṇotkaṭaḥ prahāsaś ca śvetaśīrṣaś ca nandakaḥ
english: Haṃsaja, Paṅkadigdhāṅga, and Samudronmādana, Raṇotkaṭa and Prahāsa, Śvetaśīrṣa, and Nandaka,

sanskrit: kālakaṇṭhaḥ prabhāsaś ca tathā kumbhāṇḍako 'paraḥ kālakākṣaḥ sitaś caiva bhūtalonmathanas tathā
english: Kālakaṇṭha and Prabhāsa, and the other Kumbhāṇḍaka, Kālakākṣa and Sītā, and Bhūtalonmathana likewise,

sanskrit: yajñavāhaḥ pravāhaś ca devayājī ca somapaḥ sajālaś ca mahātejāḥ krathakrāthau ca bhārata
english: Yajñavāha and Pravāha, Devayājin and Somapa, the mighty Sajāla, and Krātha and Krātha, O Bhārata,

sanskrit: tuhanaś ca tuhānaś ca citradevaś ca vīryavān madhuraḥ suprasādaś ca kirīṭī ca mahābalaḥ
english: Tuhana and Tuhāna, and the valiant Citradeva, Madhura and Suprasāda, and the mighty Kirīṭin,

sanskrit: vasano madhuvarṇaś ca kalaśodara eva ca dhamanto manmathakaraḥ sūcīvaktraś ca vīryavān
english: Vasana and Madhuvarṇa, and Kalaśodara, Dhamanta, Manmathakara, and the valiant Sūcīvaktra,

sanskrit: śvetavaktraḥ suvaktraś ca cāruvaktraś ca pāṇḍuraḥ daṇḍabāhuḥ subāhuś ca rajaḥ kokilakas tathā
english: Śvetavaktra and Suvaktra, and Cāruvaktra, Pāṇḍura, Daṇḍabāhu and Subāhu, Rajas, and Kokilaka likewise,

sanskrit: acalaḥ kanakākṣaś ca bālānām ayikaḥ prabhuḥ saṃcārakaḥ kokanado gṛdhravaktraś ca jambukaḥ
english: Acala and Kanakākṣa, and the lordly protector of children, Saṃcāraka, Kokanada, Gṛdhravaktra, and Jambuka.
